situation:
You are the customer experience manager at ZAYTOUN STREET KITCHEN, a two-year-old halal street-food business running five carts and one storefront in the hotel district. The founder (judge) has asked you to bring a recommendation on scheduling before the next quarter's payroll is set.

The first round of funding is nearly spent, and labor is the only cost the company still controls. Sales are forecast by half hour, and the forecast shows two peaks, the lunch hour in the office blocks and a late surge outside the three hotels, when guests come off delayed flights and the hotel restaurants have closed.

Those hotel guests are how the concierges came to send people over, and two of the hotels have asked about late-night trays for their own guests, which would be the first steady catering the company has had. The company also has a standing rule that no one works a cart alone after midnight.

Cutting every cart to one worker outside the two forecast peaks reaches next quarter's payroll, and it breaks the rule against working a cart alone after midnight and leaves the late hotel line waiting long enough that the concierges stop sending guests. Closing the three office-block carts and keeping two workers at the hotel carts protects that relationship, and it gives up the lunch-hour sales and the crews who work those carts.

The founder (judge) wants your recommendation on how the carts are staffed against the forecast, and wants to hear what you would tell the crews and the hotels, since either choice has to be explained to both. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of ZAYTOUN STREET KITCHEN. Business background is the same as the situation above. You know the first round of funding is nearly spent and that labor is the only cost left to move, you know the concierges at the three hotels are why the late business exists, and you wrote the rule that no one works a cart alone after midnight. You want the customer experience manager to recommend how the carts are staffed against the half-hour forecast, and to tell you how the change reaches the crews and the hotels.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would you do first to put this in place?
Who tells the crews and the hotels, and when?
